stories.head: IAB unveils framework for measuring AI's part in conversions
stories.plain: The IAB has released a common standard for crediting AI when it influences or completes a sale. This matters because without agreed measurement, brands can't compare AI-driven results across vendors or channels. A shared attribution framework will shape how marketing AI tools are bought and evaluated — and who gets paid when a bot closes a deal.

stories.head: HubSpot brings back co-founder Brian Halligan as CEO to rebuild around AI
stories.plain: Yamini Rangan is out after five years; Brian Halligan returns pledging to rebuild HubSpot's product, go-to-market, and culture around AI. HubSpot is a platform used by hundreds of thousands of businesses, so a CEO-level strategic pivot to AI will ripple through how mid-market companies buy and use marketing technology.

stories.head: Adobe expands AI stack with Google models, custom Disney models, and agentic marketing tools
stories.plain: Adobe is adding Google's models and bespoke Disney models to its AI stack while rolling out agentic tools to coordinate content and marketing workflows. This shows the enterprise AI content market consolidating around multi-model platforms, with brand-specific fine-tuning becoming a competitive differentiator for large buyers.

stories.head: ActiveCampaign opens Active Intelligence to any tool via Model Context Protocol
stories.plain: ActiveCampaign now lets marketers connect Google Ads, LinkedIn, Webflow, Airtable, or any MCP server to its AI layer, then run campaigns the agent designs. MCP as an open standard for agentic tool-calling is a structural shift in how marketing platforms integrate — this is an early real-world implementation buyers should watch.

stories.head: Optimove: how to retain the customer relationship when the buyer is an AI agent
stories.plain: Optimove's piece tackles what happens to loyalty and personalization when an AI agent — not a person — browses and buys on a shopper's behalf. It raises concrete questions about how engagement platforms must adapt when the 'customer' in the journey is itself a bot, a governance and architecture challenge that is arriving fast.

stories.head: IAB unveils framework for measuring AI's part in conversions
stories.plain: The IAB is proposing a common standard for crediting AI-assisted conversions — deciding how much of a sale belongs to an AI agent versus a human-driven touchpoint. This directly shapes how budgets are allocated, how vendors prove ROI, and how the whole industry agrees to measure AI's commercial role.

stories.head: HubSpot brings back co-founder Brian Halligan as CEO to rebuild around AI
stories.plain: HubSpot's board replaced Yamini Rangan with founder Halligan, citing a need to rebuild product, go-to-market, and culture around AI. A major platform reshaping around AI strategy affects how tens of thousands of marketers buy and use their core marketing and CRM tools.

stories.head: Connecting with shoppers when the buyer is not human — Optimove
stories.plain: As AI shopping agents increasingly make purchase decisions on behalf of consumers, brands must rethink how they present offers and maintain relationships. This piece explains what it means for customer engagement when the 'customer' doing the browsing is itself an AI agent — a structural shift in martech strategy.

stories.head: ActiveCampaign opens Active Intelligence to MCP servers and third-party tools
stories.plain: ActiveCampaign now lets marketers plug any tool — Google Ads, LinkedIn, Airtable, or any MCP-compatible server — into its AI layer so agents can run cross-channel campaigns using live business context. MCP adoption as a connective standard is a meaningful architectural shift in how agentic martech stacks are assembled.

stories.head: Sitecore launches MarketingIQ to connect AI discovery insights with content execution
stories.plain: Sitecore's new MarketingIQ tool links AI search visibility data directly to content and campaign execution, letting brands see where they appear in AI-generated answers and act on those gaps without leaving the platform. It is one of the first martech products to close the loop between GEO insight and campaign action.

month.skicker: 30-day synthesis · the shape underneath the feed

themes.head: The Agentic Commerce Takeover: When the Buyer Isn't Human
body: AI agents are increasingly acting as autonomous buyers, researchers, and decision-makers on behalf of consumers — a shift that upends how brands think about the "customer journey." Products like ZEPIC's Neura, Jungle Scout Agents, Spangle AI's Product Intelligence 360, and G2's unified marketplace all launched this month specifically to help brands optimize for agent-driven discovery rather than human browsing.

This isn't a future trend — it's a present procurement reality. If your product data, reviews, and brand signals aren't structured for AI agent consumption, you're invisible to a growing share of purchase decisions. Marketers must now treat machine-readable brand intelligence as a first-class asset, sitting alongside creative and copy.

themes.head: Autonomous CRM & Execution: Agents Replace Workflow Rules
body: The classic rule-based marketing automation playbook — if-this-then-that sequences, drip campaigns, static lead scoring — is being retired and replaced by agentic systems that reason, adapt, and act without human triggers. Launches this month from 5.Y (GLUCOSE 4.0 autonomous CRM), ActiveCampaign's Active Intelligence, and Sitecore's MarketingIQ all share the same design philosophy: replace brittle rules with continuous AI judgment.

The strategic decision this forces is where humans stay in the loop. The Aampe/MoEngage CEO framing is useful: agents handle execution, but marketers must own the purpose and guardrails. Teams that hand off execution without defining brand constraints risk drifting — a point Treasure AI's Kaz Ohta made explicitly about keeping autonomous bots on-brand at scale.

themes.head: Measuring AI's Attribution Fingerprint Before Standards Lock In
body: The IAB's new framework for crediting AI touchpoints in conversion paths is the clearest signal yet that the attribution model of the next decade is being written right now. Simultaneously, data showing that ChatGPT's paid traffic converts far worse than Google's forces an immediate re-evaluation of how AI-referred visitors are valued in existing models. Combining Marketing Mix Modeling with post-purchase surveys is gaining traction as a triangulation method when AI muddies last-click logic.

The practical danger is locking in measurement contracts or tech stacks before these standards mature. Brands that invest in flexible, multi-method attribution today — rather than doubling down on a single vendor's black box — will be able to adopt the IAB framework without a painful rip-and-replace. The cost of cheap CAC metrics that ignore quality is showing up in this month's commentary on expensive growth.

themes.head: The Data Usability Reckoning: Paying for Signals You Can't Activate
body: Three separate pieces this month converged on the same warning: organizations are acquiring data at a faster rate than their architecture can activate it. Retailer data sharpens social targeting but can silently inflate media bills; premium data sources go unused because internal systems can't ingest them; and AI platforms confidently hallucinate answers because they're pulling from siloed, unstructured knowledge bases rather than a coherent knowledge architecture.

The Thought Industries CEO's distinction between a "knowledge base" and a "knowledge architecture" is the actionable frame here. AI is only as reliable as the structure underneath it — and most martech stacks were not built with that structure in mind. Before buying another AI-enhanced platform, the month's coverage argues you must audit what data you can actually use, not what you nominally own.

themes.head: Composable, Consumer-Consented AI: Architecture Meets Trust
body: Composable martech — assembling best-of-breed components rather than relying on monolithic suites — is accelerating precisely because AI capabilities are evolving too fast for any single platform to stay current. ActiveCampaign's open integration model and the broader industry pivot toward API-first stacks reflect this. At the same time, a Shift Browser study found Americans want AI on their own terms, signaling that consumer trust and control are non-negotiable design constraints, not afterthoughts.

These two forces — architectural flexibility and user consent — are converging into a single strategic imperative: build systems that can swap AI components as the market matures, while giving consumers visible control over how their data fuels those systems. Teams still evaluating monolithic AI platform purchases should weigh this month's pre-purchase checklist guidance heavily before signing.
ev: Agile Brand · Americans want AI on own terms

month.takeaway: Every major move this month — from autonomous CRM launches to the IAB's attribution framework — points to the same inflection point: the marketing stack is being re-engineered from the ground up for a world where AI agents are both the operators of campaigns and the targets of them, and teams that treat this as a tooling upgrade rather than an architectural rethink will find themselves optimizing for a buyer experience that no longer exists.
